title: Equivalences induce equivalences of module objects; module objects in finite G-sets
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. For a category $\mathcal C$ with finite products and a final object, a *$\Lambda$-module object* of $\mathcal C$ is an object $A$ with morphisms $+:A\times A\to A$, $0:*\to A$, $-:A\to A$ and $\lambda\cdot:A\to A$ ($\lambda\in\Lambda$) satisfying the axioms of a left $\Lambda$-module written as commutative diagrams; morphisms are the morphisms of $\mathcal C$ commuting with these maps. Write $\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda(\mathcal C)$ for this category.

1. Let $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an equivalence of categories, both with finite products and final objects. Then $\Phi$ preserves finite products and the final object, and $A\mapsto\Phi(A)$, with the structure maps $\Phi(+)$, $\Phi(0)$, $\Phi(-)$, $\Phi(\lambda\cdot)$ transported along the canonical isomorphisms $\Phi(A\times A)\cong\Phi(A)\times\Phi(A)$ and $\Phi(*)\cong *$, is an equivalence $\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda(\mathcal D)$ whose underlying functor is $\Phi$ on objects and morphisms.
2. Let $G$ be a topological group and $G\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ the category of finite sets with a continuous action of $G$ (finite sets discrete) and equivariant maps. Then $\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda(G\text{-}\mathbf{Set})$ is isomorphic to the category of finite left $\Lambda$-modules $M$ with an action of $G$ by $\Lambda$-linear automorphisms for which $G\times M\to M$ is continuous ($M$ discrete), with $G$-equivariant $\Lambda$-linear maps: a module object is the finite $G$-set with its structure maps as module operations, which are $G$-equivariant exactly when $G$ acts $\Lambda$-linearly.

source.place: Lemma 0DV5 (etale-cohomology, Section 59.65), proof of parts (2)-(3): 'The equivalence in (1) sends products to products and hence sends + to an addition on the corresponding finite pi_1-set. Since pi_1-modules are the same thing as pi_1-sets with a compatible abelian group structure we obtain (2). Part (3) is proved in exactly the same way.'

proof.text: An equivalence of categories preserves all finite limits up to canonical isomorphism, hence it carries the chosen binary products and final object to products and a final object. Apply the functor to each operation map of a Lambda-module object and conjugate by these canonical isomorphisms. Applying the functor to each commutative diagram expressing a module axiom gives the corresponding diagram in the target, and the quasi-inverse transports structures back; naturality shows that maps commuting with the operations are carried precisely to maps commuting with the transported operations. Thus the induced functor on Lambda-module objects is an equivalence and its underlying functor is Phi.

proof.text: In the category of finite sets with continuous G-action, a Lambda-module object consists of a finite set A equipped with equivariant maps for addition, zero, negation and scalar multiplication satisfying the module diagrams. These maps make A a finite left Lambda-module, and equivariance says exactly that every element of G acts by a Lambda-linear automorphism. Conversely, a finite left Lambda-module with a continuous Lambda-linear G-action has all these operations equivariant, so it defines a Lambda-module object; the two constructions are inverse on objects and on equivariant linear maps.

lean.statement: theorem equivalence_induces_internalModules (R : Type r) [Ring R] {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [HasFiniteProducts C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [HasFiniteProducts D] (e : C ≌ D) : PreservesFiniteProducts e.functor ∧ PreservesLimit (Functor.empty.{0} C) e.functor ∧ ∃ E : InternalModule R C ≌ InternalModule R D, E.functor ⋙ InternalModule.forget R D = InternalModule.forget R C ⋙ e.functor ∧ (∀ A : InternalModule R C, HEq (E.functor.obj A).add (inv (prodComparison e.functor A.X A.X) ≫ e.functor.map A.add) ∧ HEq (E.functor.obj A).zero (inv (terminalComparison e.functor) ≫ e.functor.map A.zero) ∧ HEq (E.functor.obj A).neg (e.functor.map A.neg) ∧ ∀ a : R, HEq ((E.functor.obj A).smul a) (e.functor.map (A.smul a))) ∧ ∀ (A B : InternalModule R C) (f : A ⟶ B), HEq (E.functor.map f).val (e.functor.map f.val)
